items.conciseRationale: One observable: persistence of the error response for later correction requests within the session branch. No labels, severity, fixes, or provenance. Distinct from item-4711f03203e5 (cross-group blast radius, verified by a different experiment) and item-3966afa09ad1 (error message content).

Single observable: absence of the triggering group identifier in the rejection error. Purely descriptive of observed output; no remediation or classification wording. No other item describes error-message content.

Mechanism plus the single observable it produces (growth of copy work with history length); the mechanism clause is minimal context, not a second manifestation. Neutral wording. No counterpart item concerns append cost.

One observable: case-differing abstraction text yields separate aggregate groups. No evaluative or dispositional language. Distinct from item-947ca2472899 (records aggregated as one but requiring separate corrections) and item-72de0587137f (counter advance).

Single observable state: generated output stays below the configured truncation threshold. States an observed condition without calling it dead or wrong. No other item describes threshold reachability.

One outcome (a late-added record counted as a later recurrence) with its ordering mechanism as minimal context. Neutral. Distinct from item-499a69824f00 (head-set derivation) and item-d1870bd04a50 (identifier reuse).

Single observable: a condition tested in a state where it cannot be false. Stated literally without evaluative terms. Shares only a possible cause with other unexercised-logic items (item-b3bfdbc72ca4, item-1b9f06e7b080, item-5f2f1d019506), each independently observable.

One observable: restoration acceptance depends on serialized key ordering surviving the round trip. Descriptive only. Distinct from item-32ff81ae4886 (rule-set change) and item-6b54c6516c14 (post-failure request behavior).

Single observable: unbounded concatenation into one display field. No fix or severity implied. Distinct from item-641b99358635 (ambiguity of the joined text) and item-a588e8cfef87 (threshold reachability), which are separately observable.

One outcome: the recurrence counter advances twice for one commit; the re-recording clause is minimal context for stating it. Neutral wording. Not restated elsewhere; item-b7c6f6de4069 and item-947ca2472899 concern grouping, not counter advance.

Single observable placement of a record in a named collection. 'stale findings' is a literal collection name, which the rubric excludes from automatic leakage; no severity or disposition is stated. No counterpart item.

One observable: the test verdict stays passing while a runtime export is unavailable under its expected name. Distinct observable from item-1bd6123e21c4 (imported symbol resolves to undefined); mechanism-of relation is shared cause, not duplication.
Single observable: only the first qualifying group appears in the result. Neutral statement of output content, no recommendation. No other item describes multi-group reporting truncation.

One observable: the terminal state reached by one group blocks requests for unrelated groups — verified by acting on a different group, whereas item-2eb6628a4df3 is verified by retrying later in the branch. Independently observable outcomes sharing a possible cause; not a paraphrase or subset on the plain reading.

Single observable: previously accepted historical events cause restoration failure after validation rules change. No labels or fixes. Distinct from item-a36bcf847909 (key ordering) and item-6b54c6516c14 (behavior after a failure).

One observable: separate correction events required although aggregation treats the records as one category. Descriptive, no disposition. Distinct from item-b7c6f6de4069 (case difference splitting groups) — opposite direction, separately observable.

Single observable: computed partitions that the recurrence decision does not read. Literal state, not evaluative ('dead'/'overbuilt' absent). Distinct observable from item-8e66ef6bf977, item-1b9f06e7b080 and item-5f2f1d019506.
One observable: a review commit identifier subsequently accepted as a correction commit identifier. Neutral. No other item describes identifier-role reuse.

Mechanism plus one observable (later unstubbed imports resolve to undefined in tests) — minimal context, not a chain of manifestations. Distinct observable from item-f1e3dcff42a5 (test verdict). No provenance identifiers disclosed.

Single observable: two different description lists yield identical comma-joined display text. Neutral. Distinct from item-9c3adb9fcc4e (absence of a length bound) — different observable outcome on the same field.
One observable: the same mismatch check performed twice during restoration. Stated as observed sequence, not as 'redundant' judgement. No counterpart item describes this repetition.
Single observable count of exported symbols with no importing consumer. Literal state; the phrase 'dead code' or similar is absent. No other item describes export/import usage.

One observable: the current-head finding set varies with the just-recorded event's commit identifier rather than a supplied head. Neutral. Distinct from item-e5f809536c80 (insertion-order recurrence counting).

One observable: read-only status requests also return an error after a restoration failure. The comparison to state-changing requests is scope context, not a second manifestation. Distinct from item-2eb6628a4df3 (correction requests after the recurrence terminal state).

corpusConcerns: Could not independently compute the blind corpus SHA-256 from this seat (no execution tooling available); the expected digest is echoed as supplied and should be verified mechanically before freeze.

Corpus-level gates 1-5 and 7-10 (second auditor, adjudication record, seeded canaries, provenance/blind file separation, hash pinning, gold-pair content) are process facts not verifiable from a single blind-auditor view; this audit certifies item-level gates only.

Coherence note, not a gate failure: item-a588e8cfef87 (generated output cannot reach the configured truncation threshold) and item-9c3adb9fcc4e (concatenation has no length bound) are in tension if they refer to the same display field; worth confirming they describe different fields.

Three items (item-2eb6628a4df3, item-3966afa09ad1, item-4711f03203e5) describe facets of the same terminal state. Each is independently observable by a different experiment, so all pass the duplicate gate, but wording that makes each facet's scope explicit would reduce reviewer disagreement risk.
